chapter_title: Also concerning the Catechumen; shall he be saved

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The mark of one fully being introduced into a new life is this: within the person there is truth conjoined with the good it is meant to serve, yet it is held as though not one’s own possession. The whole outward condition is regarded as a temporary arrangement granted for a time, not as a permanent dwelling. All associations of kinship and companionship are valued only so far as they are necessary for the present progress, like passing connections permitted along the way, known to be loosened afterward. The knowledges, skills, and external supports used for a season are understood to be taken back into their proper order when their use is finished. Therefore such a person treats these things as capacities entrusted for service: receiving them, being helped by them for a time, and then yielding them back without fastening the heart on them. 

When such people are released from the outermost life, they continue according to the ruling love they have acquired, are led onward through an intermediate state, and are introduced into a more interior life. There they undergo purification in higher degrees: whatever is incompatible with heaven is removed, and whatever has come to maturity is taken up into the living order. In the same way, the good of charity that has proceeded from genuine love is received by those who can bear it, is freed from what clung to it from lower motives, is diversified into many forms of use, and is admitted into the life that endures. So too, the inner life of those being formed who do not return into another outward state is received, purified, and elevated according to the same pattern.

Everyone who has accepted inward expectation and trust, who has truly distinguished what enlightens from what obscures, and who has been granted perception of the secrets by which the inner person lives, has also received conjunction with peace from Divine Wisdom.

What remains that is still disordered is brought into examination; there is painful correction and repayment according to the quality of the evils. Afterward comes purification, in a higher or lower state as is required, according to the worth of the life actually lived. Thus the person is cleansed, renewed, and invested with what is fitting; then the person is brought into a formed spiritual identity receptive of light, and is raised into a state of rest, so that the inmost love becomes the abiding possession.

All of this is from the first proceeding illumination: the primary light that grants understanding through wisdom, together with the fullness of its interior knowledge.

paragraph_translations.translation: The mark of one fully being introduced into a new life is this: within the person there is truth conjoined with the good it is meant to serve, yet it remains as though not possessed as one’s own. The whole outward condition is counted as a temporary arrangement granted for a time, not as a settled dwelling. The states of kinship and companionship surrounding such a one are regarded as useful only for the present progress, like passing connections allowed along the way, known to be separated afterward. The knowledges, abilities, and external supports that were employed for a season are understood to be taken away and restored to their proper order. To such a person they are like capacities entrusted for use: one receives them, is served by them for a time, and afterward yields them back without placing confidence in them or storing the heart in them.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the description of the regenerate attitude toward externals as borrowed for use, not owned.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Woman” resists a single fixed rendering; taken here as truth conjoined to good within the person, yet held as not one’s own. “Gold and silver and utensils” treated as goods, truths, and instrumental knowledges/skills used in the external life.

paragraph_translations.translation: When such people are released from the outermost life, they continue onward according to the way they have chosen and are led through an intermediate state into a more interior life. There they are purified in higher degrees, and whatever has come to maturity for heaven is taken up. In the same way, the good of charity that is transferred into those who can receive it is changed into many forms of use, purified of what clung to it from lower things, and admitted into the living order. So too, the inner life of those being formed who do not return into another outward state is received and elevated according to the same pattern of purification and admission.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by moving from the attitude toward externals to the soul’s process after release from the outer life.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Heavens/place above” rendered as higher degrees/intermediate state. “Fruit ripening” rendered as maturity for heaven being taken up. “Alms-offering to the elect” rendered as charity’s good received by those receptive of heaven.

paragraph_translations.translation: Everyone who has received inward expectation and trust, who has separated what enlightens from what obscures, and who has been granted perception of the hidden things by which the inner life is truly alive, has received conjunction with peace from Divine Wisdom.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from process-description to a direct statement of the gift granted to those who discern and receive.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Right hand of peace” rendered as conjunction with peace. “Light Mind” rendered as Divine Wisdom.

paragraph_translations.translation: What remains that is still out of order is brought into examination; there is painful correction and repayment according to the evils. Afterward comes purification, in a higher or lower state as is required. One is purified according to the worth of the deeds, cleansed, renewed, and invested with what is fitting. Then a stable spiritual identity receptive of light is formed, and the person is raised into a state of rest, so that whatever the inmost love has been becomes the abiding possession.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the post-examination purification into renewal and elevation into rest.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Above or below” rendered as higher or lower state. “Sculpted a light image” rendered as formation of a stable spiritual identity receptive of light.

paragraph_translations.translation: This is from the first proceeding illumination: the primary light that grants understanding through wisdom, together with the fullness of its interior knowledge.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by naming the originating source of the understanding described throughout.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Riches” rendered as fullness/abundance of interior knowledge.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coheres as a single instruction on regeneration: detachment from externals, continuation after release, purification, reception of peace, and elevation into rest. The voice is consistent; the only mild strain is the dense cluster of material images in ¶3, especially “woman,” which admits more than one plausible spiritual function.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: a coherent functional teaching by enacted metaphors (house-rental, travelers, borrowed vessels) describing detachment from externals. The spiritual reading did not stumble here except for one polyvalent symbol (“woman”), which is a normal correspondential ambiguity, not an insertion.
findings.evidence: Text works by function/use: externals are temporary and instrumental—“living in a house for rent by days and months… necessary as foreign people… borrowed vessels; [he] takes them, is served by them, and afterwards gives them to their owner.” This yields the reading’s core: “externals as borrowed for use, not owned.” The reading’s only noted strain—“‘Woman’ resists a single fixed rendering”—is expected in correspondential language where one image can carry several lawful functions (truth/affection/church) without changing voice or breaking narrative.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential continuation: post-mortem process is taught by functional analogies (travel, purification, fruit ripening, alms transference). No narrative seam; the catechumen theme remains active.
findings.evidence: The paragraph stays in process/states: “come forth from their body… travel… pass by… go in to the life… purified… plucked just as a fruit that ripens.” The alms simile also teaches by function (transfer/purification/admission): “alms-offering that passes over to the elect… purified… goes in to the land of the living.” The spiritual reading tracks this smoothly (“intermediate state… purification… maturity… charity… diversified into many forms of use”), and reports no ‘doesn’t fit’ moment—evidence against administrative overlay.

findings.diagnosis: Potential micro-seam but not disruptive: a brief gnomic summary (‘everyone who… has received…’) that condenses the prior process into a criterion and gift. It remains correspondential (states of discernment; reception from Light Mind) and does not introduce jurisdictional cataloguing. This is a rhetorical shift, not a foreign voice insertion.
findings.evidence: The text moves from narrative/process to a present-tense generalization: “Every person who has received the hope and the faith… separated the light from the darkness… perceived the mysteries… received the right hand of peace from the Light Mind.” The reading notes a “SHIFT… to a direct statement,” but it still derives spiritual sense from inner functions (discernment, perception, reception), not from ranks/territories. No named officials, stations, or inventories appear.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential eschatological mechanics: examination → blows/retribution → purification above/below → cleansing/adornment → ‘sculpted’ light image → ascent/rest. This is functional transformation language, not administrative governance.
findings.evidence: Strong process chain with bodily-craft metaphors: “questioned… receive blows… purified… cleansed and washed and adorned… sculpted a light image… glides up… land of rest,” concluding with the functional proverb “where his heart is, his treasure also will be there.” The spiritual reading follows without forcing (“painful correction… purification… formed spiritual identity… raised into rest”), indicating no narrative break that would suggest insertion.

findings.diagnosis: Likely closing colophon-like doxological tag, but still compatible with the substrate: it names the source principle (‘first light’/Mind/knowledge) rather than introducing administrative machinery. Reads as a thematic capstone rather than an intrusive taxonomy expansion.
findings.evidence: Text: “the first light, the one that brings understanding through the Mind and [the] riches of its knowledge.” The reading treats it as the originating illumination behind the whole instruction. No new agents, ranks, or territorial controls are introduced; it does not disrupt the catechumen narrative.

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative-voice intrusions detected in the restored text. 5 findings confirm coherent correspondential substrate throughout. The only ‘stumble’ noted by the spiritual reading (polyvalence of “woman” in ¶3) is a genuine correspondential ambiguity, not evidence of insertion. Recommendations: excise 0, annotate 0, none 5.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: The sign of that perfect catechumen is this: You shall find the woman in the house with him, and beside him she is like these strangers. His house, in his reckoning, shall be like these lodging houses. He says: I am living in a house for rent by days and months. His brothers and his relatives shall be, in his reckoning, necessary as foreign people who take up with him, while travelling on the road with him. He [knows that, after a time,] they will separate from him, and each one [of them] may [take] the gold and the silver and the utensils of the [same] house. To him, they shall be like borrowed vessels; [he] takes them, is served by them, and afterwards gives them to their owner. He does not set his trust on them, nor his treasure.

When, however, they come forth from their body, they travel on their way and pass by in the place above, and go in to the life. They shall be purified in the heavens, and they are plucked just as a fruit that ripens is plucked from the tree. In just the same way, this alms-offering that passes over to the elect is given likeness in many forms. It is purified and goes in to the land of the living. Similarly, the souls of the catechumens who shall not enter (another) body resemble (the alms).

Every person who has received the hope and the faith and has separated the light from the darkness, and has perceived the mysteries of the living soul, he has received the right hand of peace from the Light Mind

As for the rest, he shall be questioned about a single part; and receive blows for (those sins) and retribution. Afterwards he is purified, whether indeed above or below. He shall be purified according to the worth of his deeds, and cleansed and washed and adorned. Afterwards, he is sculpted a light image; and [he glides]es up and reaches the land of rest, so that the place where his heart is, his treasure also will be there.
the first light, the one that brings understanding through the Mind and [the] riches of its knowledge.

changes_summary: No changes were made. All critic recommendations were “none” (Findings 1–5), with no excisions or annotations required.
